title: Base N7 and early 193 nm immersion lithography

questions.reason: The production link is supported at the 193 nm technique level by TSMC’s R&D disclosures and earnings call, a contemporary Semiconductor Engineering account, and industry analysis identifying ArF immersion. The link leaves the inheritance of any specific 40 nm recipe unresolved.

The foundry identifies an ASML immersion prototype used for the split wafer trial. The scanner maker documents its prototype and pre-production immersion programme, its collaboration with TSMC and the use of its early equipment for TSMC’s successful trial.
The existing 2004 feasibility and 2008 40 nm use events omitted the distinct N45LP process qualification and delivery dated by TSMC to Q3 2007.

findings: At the equipment level, ASML demonstrated 193 nm immersion imaging on the AT:1150i in October 2003. Its 2003 conference presentation identifies the test patterns and its retrospective describes a specific technical adaptation of the dry dual-stage design.

At the process level, TSMC verified its SRAM trial after exposure at ASML and completion at TSMC in 2004. N45LP qualification and delivery followed in Q3 2007. The existing Q4 2008 event covers both 40 nm variants.

The 2015 R&D account identifies new resist and mask development for 7 nm. TSMC’s 2012 report traces earlier 193 nm immersion-scanner improvements aimed at multiple patterning. The 2014 report explicitly relates patterning from 20 and 16 nm to the 10 nm immersion development.
frontier: Look for the TSMC trial presentation from the 1 December 2004 Cymer Lithography Symposium or a tool log to identify the exact ASML prototype used on the TSMC split.

Follow the documented modification of the dry ASML TWINSCAN AT:1150 lens and body to early ArF dry projection scanners. ASML’s 20th-anniversary chapter 6 gives the adaptation and identifies Philips and ZEISS roles. Original equipment and customer records are needed to date the dry platform milestone and trace any predecessor or transfer.

Inspect a full 2016 Wu et al. IEDM paper (DOI 10.1109/IEDM.2016.7838333) and TechInsights N7 process-flow records for the layers, tools and any direct transfer of recipes between 10 nm and production base N7.

screen: Searched discoveries, sources, link targets, leads and the earlier chip audit for TWINSCAN, AT:1150i, XT:1250i, 193 nm, immersion, ArF and projection lithography. Existing records cover TSMC integration and base N7, each extended in place. The existing Alpha Demo is EUV. The nineteenth-century Zeiss objectives show an optical analogy and do not identify a transfer into this semiconductor programme.
limits: Sampled published technical and operator documents through 17 November 2026. Prototype imaging, functional-device trials, foundry qualification and production are distinct. No worldwide priority, full equipment list, exact scanner on the 2004 TSMC wafer batch, or recipe-level lineage into N7 is assigned.
